video_caption: The video segment opens with a black screen before transitioning to a top-down view of a person's dark-skinned hands holding a black smartphone with a white screen displaying app icons, resting on a light-colored, speckled surface. The right thumb taps the Facebook app icon. Subsequently, a white overlay featuring a blue thumbs-up icon, a red "SUBSCRIBE" button, and a black bell icon appears at the bottom of the screen. The right thumb taps the "SUBSCRIBE" button, which then changes to a gray "SUBSCRIBED" with an animated thumbs-up and ringing bell, indicating a subscription action. The phone then displays the Facebook app, specifically a "Groups" feed, and the hands scroll through various posts, some containing images and others text, such as a post asking, "Hello, would you allow popsi company to put a small sticker on your vehicle for £275 a month?". Throughout the scrolling, a lower-third graphic is present at the bottom left, displaying "Timothy Adjokatse" above "Software Developer."

The video begins with an overhead shot of a person with dark skin interacting with a black smartphone placed on a light-colored, speckled round table. Their hands are actively scrolling through a social media feed on the phone, which displays various images and text posts. A red "SUBSCRIBE" button with a thumbs-up and bell icon is visible on the right side of the screen; it then animates to show "SUBSCRIBED" (meaning the user has subscribed). A text overlay appears on the video that reads "How to convert a Facebook profile to a Facebook page.", providing context for the content. The scene then transitions to a direct screen recording of a smartphone displaying the Facebook app interface. The top of the screen shows a "What's on your mind?" search bar and tabs for "Stories," "Reels," and "Rooms," with "Rooms" currently selected. Below, there's an option to "Create room" and a live room with "Abena Manokekame LIVE 21 30 Manokekame" and a "Listen" button. As the screen scrolls down, a post from "Nānā Teā" appears, asking "You get light?" with comments below. Further scrolling reveals a sponsored ad from "React fellows" with "PRICE INCREASE $299" crossed out and "$249" below it, along with a "FULL ACCESS" icon and "3 DAYS LEFT!". This ad promotes an "Online Summit for React JS Developers" from "events.geeke.us" with a "Book Now" button. The final visible post is from "Doe-Quarshie Michael," stating he "is feeling sad at Madina. 1 hour ago Accra, Ghana" and "BREAKING NEWS: Black Sherif sued by his Former Manager!!..".

The video opens with a silver laptop appearing and then opening on a white background to reveal a black screen, which then displays the "AdJoTech" logo featuring a yellow square, blue teardrop, and red triangle forming an abstract 'A'. After the logo disappears and the screen turns white again, the scene transitions to a smartphone screen showing the Facebook app, where an advertisement for a "React Global Summit" displays "PRICE INCREASE! $299 $249 FULL ACCESS 3 DAYS LEFT!". An animated red arrow guides the viewer to click on the profile icon at the top right, and a white interactive button with a blue thumbs-up and the text "SUBSCRIBE" (red) appears and is clicked, changing to "SUBSCRIBED" (blue) with a blue bell icon, then the arrow points to the three-bar menu icon. Following a voice prompt, the menu opens, and the screen scrolls down to "Settings & privacy", which is then expanded. The voice directs the user to click on "Settings", leading to a page where "Personal information" is highlighted, and the "SUBSCRIBE" button is clicked again. The "Personal information" screen appears, and "Name Timothy Adjokatse" is highlighted, prompting another click on the "SUBSCRIBE" button. Finally, the "Name" editing page is shown with fields for "First name", "Middle name", and "Surname" pre-filled with "Timothy" and "Adjokatse", along with a note about name change restrictions, and the "SUBSCRIBE" button is clicked once more before the video ends.

The video segment opens on a mobile screen displaying the Facebook "Name" settings page, where fields for "First name" (Timothy), "Middle name," and "Surname" (Adjokatse) are visible. A note states, "Please note: If you change your name on Facebook, you can't change it again for 60 days. Don't add any unusual capitalisation, punctuation, characters or random words. Learn more." The "Learn more" link is highlighted by a red box. The screen then transitions to the Facebook Help Centre, displaying "What names are allowed on Facebook?" This page lists restrictions on names and, after scrolling down, shows "If your name follows our standards and you're still having trouble changing it, find out why." The "find out why" link is highlighted. Clicking this link leads to a "Why can't I change my name on Facebook?" Help Centre page. The user scrolls down, revealing steps on how to change a name and then a crucial note: "If you're still having trouble with changing your name, you can fill in this form to request a name change and confirm your name." This "fill in this form" link is highlighted. Upon clicking, the screen transitions to a "Changing Your Name" form, which includes input fields for "New first name," "New middle name (optional)," and "New surname." As the user scrolls further down the form, a significant red box highlights the following text: "Note that Timelines are for personal use only. If you're trying to change your account name in order to represent a business or organization, or to represent yourself as a public figure, you should create a Page or convert this account to a Page." A "Send" button is visible at the bottom of the form.

The video segment displays a mobile phone screen against a solid blue background, showing a Facebook name change form. The form includes fields for "Reason for this change" (Choose one), "Your documents" (Choose files No file chosen with an icon), and "Contact email address" (Provide an email only you have access to). A red rectangular outline highlights a crucial note at the bottom of the form, which states: "Note that Timelines are for personal use only. If you're trying to change your account name in order to represent a business or organization, or to represent yourself as a public figure, you should create a Page or convert this account to a Page." (The meaning is that personal Facebook profiles are not for commercial or public figure use; dedicated Pages should be used instead). Below this text is a blue "Send" button. As a voice-over discusses converting an account to a page, a red "SUBSCRIBE" button with a white thumbs-up and bell icon appears on the right side of the screen at 00:26, briefly changing to "SUBSCRIBED" and showing a ringing bell animation before reverting to "SUBSCRIBE".

The video begins with a smartphone screen displaying a Facebook interface for a name change request, set against a dark blue background. The white content area shows input fields for "Reason for this change," "Your documents" (with "Choose files No file chosen" and a grid icon), and "Contact email address." Below these, a "Note" is displayed, stating: "Note that Timelines are for personal use only. If you're trying to change your account name in order to represent a business or organization, or to represent yourself as a public figure, you should create a Page or convert this account to a Page." The last part, "convert this account to a Page," is highlighted with a red rectangular box. A voiceover instructs, "Convert this account to a page. So this is a profile page and we actually want to convert it to what? A page. So just click on that." A finger taps the highlighted text. The screen then briefly transitions to a dark loading screen with a white spinner and a grid icon, before displaying a new Facebook Help Centre page. This page is titled "Pages | Facebook Help Centre" and features a large "Pages" heading with a blue thumbs-up icon next to it. The content provides information about managing Facebook Pages, including details on how to "like or follow a Page," "create a Page," and sections like "Learn how to:" which list actions such as inviting people, assigning roles, adding a call-to-action button, and seeing Page Insights. A "SUBSCRIBED" button, along with thumbs-up and bell icons, is visible on the right side of the video frame.

The video displays a mobile phone screen showing the Facebook "Help Centre" interface against a solid blue background. The top of the screen shows the time "10:48" along with battery and signal indicators. The main content of the screen is a "Pages" help article, with the heading "Pages" prominently displayed. Text on the screen reads: "Pages that you manage may be in the new Pages experience. Learn more about new Pages." Below that, it states: "You can like or follow a Page to get updates from businesses, organisations and public figures. Anyone with a Facebook account can create a Page or help manage one, as long as they have a role on the Page." Further down, under "Learn how to:", two bullet points are visible: "Invite people to like your Page or share another Page with your friends." and "Assign roles for your Page to let other people help manage it." A thumb occasionally appears on the screen, gesturing down the page. Towards the end of the segment, an animated cursor clicks a white "LIKE" button, then a red "SUBSCRIBE" button (with the text "SUBSCRIBE" in white), followed by a bell icon with radiating lines, located in the bottom right corner of the video frame.

The video displays a mobile phone screen on a solid blue background, showing the Facebook Help Centre interface. At the top, the navigation breadcrumbs read "Pages | Facebook Help Centre". Below the "Help Centre" title, a list of categories is visible: "Publishing", "Messaging", "Insights", "Banning and moderation", and "Fix a problem". A red rectangular highlight appears around the question "Was this helpful?" at the bottom of the screen, with "Yes" and "No" buttons. The user taps "No", which reveals a new section titled "What went wrong?" offering options: "The information is confusing", "The solution doesn't work", "I don't like the product or policy", and "Other". The user selects "The solution doesn't work", after which a "Can you say more?" section appears. This section includes a disclaimer ("Bear in mind that this form is for feedback only and you won't receive a reply. Please don't include personal information about you or someone else. Learn more about how to report something to Facebook."), an "Optional" text input field, and a "Submit" button. Towards the end of the segment, a red "LIKE SUBSCRIBE" graphic with a thumbs-up icon and a notification bell icon slides in from the right, partially covering the "Submit" button.

The video segment opens at 0:00 showing a smartphone screen displaying the Facebook Help Centre. The visible options include "messaging", "Insights", "Banning and moderation", and "Fix a problem". Below these, a section titled "Can you say more?" features a disclaimer in English: "Bear in mind that this form is for feedback only and you won't receive a reply. Please don't include personal information about you or someone else. Learn more about how to report something to Facebook." Beneath this text is an "Optional" input field and a "Submit" button. At 0:02, the screen briefly transitions to the phone's home screen, showing a grid of app icons (including WhatsApp, Messenger, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn) against a dark wallpaper with abstract red/purple and blue swirling patterns. The date "Mon, 11 Apr" and temperature "32°C" are visible in the status bar. The screen then goes dark at 0:03 before transitioning at 0:05 to a WhatsApp chat interface. Here, two image files named "fire conference.jpg" and "fire conference1.jpg" are shown, along with a blurred image indicating a "221 KB" download. Below these, a message from the user is visible: "https://www.facebook.com /360adjokatse" followed by "Hello Facebook team, I want to convert my facebook profile to a Facebook page." The user then interacts with the screen, presumably copying the Facebook profile link. At 0:08, the screen briefly returns to the home screen wallpaper before quickly reappearing on the Facebook Help Centre page at 0:10. The user then taps into the "Optional" input field within the "Can you say more?" section, causing a virtual keyboard to pop up from the bottom of the screen at 0:19.

In this video segment, a person interacts with a mobile phone screen displaying a Facebook feedback form. The form has a heading "Can you say more?" and a descriptive text "Bear in mind that this form is for feedback only and you won't receive a reply. Please don't include personal information about you or someone else. learn more about how to report something to Facebook." Below this, there's an input field labeled "Optional" and a "Submit" button. A virtual keyboard is visible at the bottom of the screen. The person pastes text into the "Optional" field, which includes a Facebook profile URL ("https://www.facebook.com/360adjokatse"), a timestamp ("[11/04, 9:50 pm]"), and a message addressed to the Facebook team: "Hello Facebook team, I want to convert my Facebook profile to a Facebook page but this is not working. Please fix it." As the text is pasted, a YouTube overlay appears in the bottom right corner showing a "SUBSCRIBE" button with a thumbs-up icon, which then changes to "SUBSCRIBED" with a bell icon. The phone screen is set against a plain blue background.

The video segment displays a smartphone screen with a Facebook interface, set against a solid blue background. The screen shows a "Fix a problem" form with the heading "Can you say more?". Below this, there's a disclaimer: "Bear in mind that this form is for feedback only and you won't receive a reply. Please don't include personal information about you or someone else. Learn more about how to report something to Facebook." (English translation: "Bear in mind that this form is for feedback only and you won't receive a reply. Please don't include personal information about you or someone else. Learn more about how to report something to Facebook."). A text box contains a URL "https://www.facebook.com/360ad" followed by the message: "Hello Facebook team, I want to convert my Facebook profile to a Facebook page but this is not working. Please fix it." (English translation: "Hello Facebook team, I want to convert my Facebook profile to a Facebook page but this is not working. Please fix it."). Below the text box is a blue "Submit" button. Further down, under the "Popular articles" heading, several links are visible, including "Resources for Page admins," "How do I report a Facebook account or Page that's pretending to be me or someone else?," "How do I add a sticker to my Page's story on Facebook?," and "Interact with Page." A virtual keyboard is at the bottom of the screen, showing a QWERTY layout with some special characters in the top row.

The video starts on a Facebook app screen titled "Confirm Your Name," displaying text that explains Facebook's identity confirmation process, including the use of trusted service providers, secure ID storage, and a 30-day deletion policy for submitted IDs (if opt-out). It also details the optional upload of a government ID, library card, or utility bill for name verification, with input fields for "Reason for this change," "Your documents" (with a "Choose files" button), and "Contact email address." At 0:02, the screen quickly swipes back, followed by a brief loading screen. From 0:04, a "Name" screen appears, showing "First name: Timothy," "Middle name," and "Surname: Adjokatse," accompanied by a "Please note" message about Facebook's name change policy, specifically the 60-day waiting period. Buttons for "Review Change" and "Cancel" are visible below. At 0:05, the screen swipes back, and from 0:07, a "Personal information" screen is displayed, listing "General" (Name: Timothy Adjokatse), "Contact info," "Identity confirmation," and "Manage account." A Twitter-like bar at the top partially reads "KALYJAY God when https://t.co/SQcFdv7E2Z." The video transitions at 0:09 to the Facebook "Menu" screen, where "Settings & privacy" is expanded to show options like "Settings," "Privacy shortcuts," "Your time on Facebook," "Device requests," "Recent ad activity," and "Mobile centre - MTN." A red "SUBSCRIBE" button with a white thumbs up and bell icon appears on the right side. From 0:11, the screen shows the Facebook app's main feed, featuring a large ad banner for a "React Global Summit" with a "PRICE INCREASE" notification (from $299 to $249, "3 DAYS LEFT!"). Below this, "Stories," "Reels," and "Rooms" sections are visible, including a live room for "Abena Manokekame." The "SUBSCRIBE" button now appears as "SUBSCRIBED" with an activated bell icon. At 0:13, the user navigates to their profile page, displaying "Timothy Adjokatse" with a profile picture of a man wearing glasses and a cover photo related to "Web Design & Development." His bio reads "God first || Youtuber || Web Developer || Digital Marketer || Entrepreneur || Software Developer." Buttons for "Add to Story," "Edit profile," and three dots are present. The user clicks on the three dots, which at 0:17 opens the "Profile settings" screen, showing various options like "Follow Settings," "Account status," "Archive," and "View as." Crucially, "Your profile link" is displayed as "https://www.facebook.com/360adjokatse" with a "Copy Link" button below it. At 0:20, the user taps "Copy Link," and a "Link copied" confirmation appears briefly at the bottom. The user then swipes back to their profile page at 0:23, and then back to the Facebook app's main feed at 0:26, where the video concludes. The "SUBSCRIBED" button remains visible throughout the latter half of the video.

The video begins with a screen recording of a mobile phone displaying the Facebook app on a dark blue background, showcasing the main feed with navigation tabs for "Stories," "Reels," and "Rooms." A "Create room" button is visible, next to an active room labeled "Abena Manokekame" with 20 out of 24 participants, and a "Listen" button. Below this, a Facebook post by "Nâna Teä" reads "You get light?" accompanied by reaction counts and comments. A red mouse pointer appears and moves to the bottom right, briefly hovering over an orange camera icon and a grid icon before moving towards a "SUBSCRIBE" button overlaid on the screen. The pointer clicks the "SUBSCRIBE" button, changing it to "SUBSCRIBED" with an adjacent bell icon. It then clicks the bell icon, revealing a menu with options "All," "Personalized," and "None," and selects "All." The pointer subsequently clicks a pause icon on the Facebook screen, leading to a transition to an animated end screen. This end screen, set against a dark blue background, first displays the text "THANKS FOR WATCHING" in light blue and green, followed by "PLEASE HIT" and a large light green circle containing a white thumbs-up icon. The next animation shows "SHARE &" and a similar green circle with a white sharing icon. Finally, a red YouTube play button appears, alongside the text "SUBSCRIBE," both of which then disappear, leaving a small, pulsating purple and blue bar that fades out.
